theme: Saying what you can and can't do — the potential form
intro: Reshape any verb into its potential form to say you are able to do something.

grammar.title: The potential form (可能形)

rules.label: る-verbs (ichidan)
rules.detail: drop る, add られる
examples: たべる → たべられる (can eat)
みる → みられる (can see)

rules.label: う-verbs (godan)
examples: はなす → はなせる (can speak)

rules.label: Irregulars
examples: くる → こられる (can come)

grammar.bigPoint: With the potential form the object particle を usually becomes が: さしみを たべる → さしみが たべられる.

examples.jp: にほんごが すこし はなせます。
examples.en: I can speak a little Japanese.

examples.jp: からいものが たべられますか。

note: Every potential-form verb conjugates like a る-verb (ichidan): はなせる → はなせます / はなせない / はなせて. Note いける also means 'that works / not bad' casually.

selfCheck.q: 書く (かく, to write) is an う-verb. Put it in the potential form and say 'I can write hiragana.' (Remember を→が.)
selfCheck.a: かく → かける. → ひらがなが かけます。 (Hiragana ga kakemasu.)
